posts.text: Speaking on Thursday's episode of The Grand Standoff: Iran and the World, Professor Mohammad Marandi said he did not believe Iran takes Saudi Arabia's threats seriously. Iran's regime is so desperate for cash it's printing increasingly worthless rials just to avoid missing payroll for its security forces, government workers, and pensioners.

But printing money isn't the same as paying people when the currency has collapsed.

At 2.72 million rials to the dollar, the regime can print salaries. It can't print purchasing power.

با دلار ۲.۷۲ میلیون ریالی، حکومت می‌تواند حقوق چاپ کند، ولی قدرت خرید نه.

Four Hamas operatives were killed in strikes in the southern Gaza Strip on Wednesday, the military announces.

One strike in Khan Younis killed Mohammed Alyan al-Bayouk, identified by the IDF as a member of Hamas's elite Nukhba Force.

The Saudi newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat reported earlier that the Shin Bet security agency called Bayouk before carrying out the strike, telling him he had to choose between being killed alongside his family or being killed alone on the roof. According to the report, Bayouk chose to go up to the roof, where he was killed.

An Israeli soldier has been arrested and charged with carrying out a slew of espionage tasks on behalf of Iran in exchange for cryptocurrency, authorities announce.

The soldier had been arrested in September following a joint investigation carried out by the Shin Bet, Israel Police, and Military Police, which suspected him of committing "grave security offenses, including maintaining contact with Iranian intelligence operatives and carrying out tasks under their direction."

Today, military prosecutors filed an indictment charging him with passing information to the enemy with the intent to harm state security and for the benefit of the enemy, as well as contact with a foreign agent.

The Shin Bet, police, and IDF say that during his interrogation, it emerged that the soldier had maintained contact with Iranian agents for about a year, during which he provided sensitive information about his unit's military activities, the IDF's readiness and call-ups, including details about his own call-up at the outbreak of the war with Iran earlier this year.

"The investigation also found that the soldier acted with awareness of the identity of his Iranian handler," and that in exchange for the information he sent them, he received payment in cryptocurrency, the joint statement says.

The final voter turnout in Israel's national elections among IDF soldiers reached 79.9%, the military says.

The IDF says this is an increase of 6.2% compared to the previous elections in 2022.

Conscripts, career soldiers, and reservists began voting a week ago at over 890 polling stations deployed to military bases across the country and beyond Israel's borders, including at army posts in the Gaza Strip, Lebanon, and Syria.

The Israeli military issues a response to recent media reports on a major confrontation between the political leadership and IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir related to Iran.

"Regarding various reports in the Israeli and international media over the past day, which attributed various statements to the chief of staff or senior military officials, we wish to clarify: The IDF is focused on its missions and maintains a high state of alert on all fronts, in light of various warnings and the sensitivity of the current period," the military says, referring to the elections.

"The operational activities and considerations of the IDF are solely security-related, professional, matter-of-fact, and statesmanlike, and any other discourse is misleading and irrelevant," the military adds.
